variations.name: High-temperature thermal batteries (molten salt, bricks, sand, carbon blocks + TPV)
variations.description: Electric resistance heating charges cheap media — firebricks, crushed rock, sand, molten salt or carbon blocks — to 500–2,400 C, then discharges as industrial steam/heat (or electricity via thermophotovoltaics), attacking the ~20% of global emissions from industrial process heat with dirt-cheap storage materials.

companies.name: Rondo Energy
companies.what: Brick-based 'Heat Battery' delivering continuous high-pressure steam from intermittent solar/wind
companies.signal: ~$107M raised (Microsoft, Aramco MoU); world's largest 100 MWh unit entered daily commercial operation at a California fuels plant Oct 2025; five industrial-scale units deployed globally

companies.name: Antora Energy
companies.what: Modular carbon-block batteries reaching >1,500 C with optional thermophotovoltaic electricity output
companies.signal: $150M Series B (Feb 2024, BlackRock/Temasek's Decarbonization Partners), ~$244M total; 50 MW / 5 GWh system commissioning at POET bioprocessing plant, South Dakota

companies.name: Brenmiller Energy
companies.what: bGen crushed-rock thermal storage for industrial steam, including gas-turbine exhaust capture
companies.signal: NASDAQ-listed (BNRG); commissioned NYPA project at SUNY Purchase plus European industrial installs

companies.name: Kyoto Group
companies.what: Heatcube molten-salt heat battery replacing gas boilers for industrial process heat
companies.signal: Oslo-listed; 56 MWh Heatcube inaugurated at KALL Ingredients corn plant in Hungary Oct 2025; Nefco loan for international scale-up

companies.name: Polar Night Energy
companies.what: 'Sand batteries' storing heat in sand/crushed soapstone for district heating, plus a power-out pilot
companies.signal: 1 MW / 100 MWh Pornainen unit operating; contracted world-largest 2 MW / 250 MWh system for Lahti Energia (Nov 2025, complete 2027)

companies.name: EnergyNest
companies.what: Concrete 'Thermal Battery' modules for industrial power-to-heat
companies.signal: 10 MW / 40 MWh system at tesa Hamburg (52% heat electrification); 12 MWh project at Leonhard Kurz

companies.name: Kraftblock
companies.what: Up-to-1,300 C storage granulate made from recycled industrial slag for two-week duration heat storage
companies.signal: Industrial pilots including PepsiCo Netherlands fryer-heat project; German VC-backed

companies.name: Electrified Thermal Solutions
companies.what: Electrically conductive 'Joule Hive' firebricks (MIT spinout) that self-heat to ~1,800 C for the hardest industrial heat
companies.signal: DOE grant-backed; founding member of Thermal Battery Alliance (Jan 2025); first commercial demo with HWI/Calpine underway

companies.name: Fourth Power
companies.what: Liquid-tin/graphite storage at ~2,400 C discharged to electricity via thermophotovoltaic cells ('sun in a box')
companies.signal: $20M Series A+ led by Munich Re Ventures (Sep 2025), $40M total incl. DCVC and Breakthrough Energy Ventures; claims <$25/kWh-e storage cost

companies.name: MGA Thermal
companies.what: Miscibility-gap-alloy blocks storing latent heat in metal microdroplets for industrial steam
companies.signal: ~$35M raised; 5 MWh steam-integrated demonstration unit commissioned Apr 2025 (won 2025 Australian Renewable Heat Award); 180 MWh Knode project in Western Australia progressing

variations.name: Pumped thermal / Carnot batteries
variations.description: Heat pumps convert cheap electricity into a hot store (often paired with a cold store) and a heat engine reverses the cycle to regenerate power, promising multi-day storage from steel, rock and salt — but ~50-60% round-trip efficiency has kept it behind Li-ion and pushed players toward selling heat instead.

companies.name: Malta Inc
companies.what: Google X spinout storing electricity in molten salt via a heat-pump/heat-engine cycle; now also selling 300-550 C industrial heat pumps
companies.signal: 14 MW Puertollano (Spain) LDES pilot launched Jun 2025 with BBVA revenue agreement; first commercial Advanced Heat Pump at Proman methanol plant, Texas

companies.name: Stiesdal Storage
companies.what: GridScale crushed-basalt pumped thermal storage from wind pioneer Henrik Stiesdal
companies.signal: 4 MW / 10 MWh demonstrator at Rodby, Denmark since 2023; commercial rollout has been slow since

companies.name: Echogen Power Systems
companies.what: Supercritical-CO2 heat-engine cycles for electro-thermal energy storage and waste heat recovery
companies.signal: ARPA-E DAYS awardee; licenses sCO2 power cycle technology to OEMs

companies.name: MAN Energy Solutions
companies.what: ETES electro-thermal storage and very large industrial heat pumps (e.g., 50 MW Esbjerg seawater heat pump) plus Carnot-cycle turbomachinery
companies.signal: Volkswagen Group subsidiary; ETES reference plants in Denmark/Norway

companies.name: Siemens Gamesa (ETES program)
companies.what: Built the world's first large rock-bed electric thermal storage demo (130 MWh, Hamburg, 2019) then shelved the program — the sector's key failure datapoint
companies.signal: Demo operated ~2019-2022; program discontinued as parent retrenched

variations.white_space: Thin field for physics reasons — heat-pump/heat-engine round trips lose ~40-50% of energy, and Li-ion cost declines killed the pure power-to-power case (Siemens Gamesa quit; Malta pivoted toward industrial heat); the opening is hybrid heat-plus-power offtake and repowering retiring coal plants whose steam turbines a Carnot battery can reuse.

variations.name: Phase-change & thermochemical storage
variations.description: Stores energy in a material's melting transition (PCM — ice, salt hydrates, metal alloys) or a reversible chemical reaction (thermochemical metal oxides/salts), giving compact, low-loss heat and cooling batteries for buildings and industry rather than bulk electricity.

companies.name: Sunamp
companies.what: Plentigrade salt-hydrate PCM 'Thermino' heat batteries replacing hot-water cylinders in homes
companies.signal: ~$28.6M raised; tens of thousands of UK/EU installs; launched low-power models for the Italian market Mar 2025

companies.name: CALMAC (Trane Technologies)
companies.what: IceBank ice-storage tanks shifting commercial-building cooling load off-peak — the mature workhorse of PCM storage
companies.signal: Thousands of buildings worldwide; acquired by Ingersoll Rand/Trane in 2016

companies.name: Nostromo Energy
companies.what: IceBrick modular ice-cell arrays retrofitted to commercial buildings for peak cooling demand response
companies.signal: Installed at flagship California hotels (e.g., Beverly Hilton); TASE-listed, pursuing US utility programs

companies.name: Phase Change Solutions
companies.what: BioPCM plant-derived phase-change materials tunable from -75 C to 175 C for buildings and cold chain
companies.signal: Commercial sales across 40+ countries; partnerships in building retrofit

companies.name: SaltX Technology
companies.what: Swedish nano-coated salt thermochemical storage developer, now commercializing an Electric Arc Calciner for zero-emission lime/cement
companies.signal: Nasdaq First North-listed; pivot from grid storage to electrified calcination is itself market evidence

companies.name: RedoxBlox
companies.what: Metal-oxide redox thermochemical modules storing heat plus chemical energy, discharging above 1,100 C for industrial heat and gas-turbine decarbonization
companies.signal: ARPA-E and Khosla Ventures-backed; founding member of the Thermal Battery Alliance (Jan 2025)

companies.name: Azelio
companies.what: Swedish aluminum-alloy PCM storage with Stirling-engine electricity output (TES.POD)
companies.signal: Filed for bankruptcy mid-2023 after failing to raise — cautionary tale for PCM power-to-power

companies.name: Ice Energy
companies.what: Ice Bear behind-the-meter ice batteries for residential/small-commercial AC
companies.signal: Filed Chapter 7 in 2019 despite utility contracts — demand-side cooling storage proved hard to finance

variations.white_space: Building-side ice/PCM is commercial, but high-temperature thermochemical storage has only a couple of credible players because reaction reversibility and cycling degradation are hard chemistry; an opening exists above ~1,000 C where sensible-heat bricks lose energy density and industrial gas users need both heat and storable chemical energy.

variations.name: Gravity storage (towers, mine shafts, rail, cranes)
variations.description: Lifts mass — composite blocks in towers, weights in disused mine shafts, rail cars on slopes, water-filled pistons — with surplus power and recovers electricity on descent; the physics is simple and degradation-free, but low energy density and high structural cost have kept it above battery prices.

companies.name: Energy Vault
companies.what: EVx gravity towers raising/lowering 24-tonne composite blocks; the only public pure-play, though US revenue has pivoted to conventional BESS
companies.signal: NYSE: NRGV; 25 MW / 100 MWh Rudong (China) system commissioned, ~9 licensed China deployments totaling 3.7+ GWh; $150M convertible note closed Mar 2026

companies.name: Gravitricity
companies.what: Weights of 500-5,000 tonnes raised and lowered in abandoned mine shafts
companies.signal: 250 kW Edinburgh demonstrator proven; agreements for projects at former mines (Finland's Pyhasalmi, US, India), still pre-commercial

companies.name: Green Gravity
companies.what: Australian developer repurposing legacy mine shafts with ore-filled weights
companies.signal: Agreements with mine owners (e.g., Woodlawn); government grant-backed, pilot stage

companies.name: ARES North America
companies.what: GravityLine — chains of weighted rail cars on a Nevada slope providing grid regulation
companies.signal: Broke ground on 50 MW merchant Pahrump Valley plant (2023) targeting Q4 2025 operation; little public confirmation since

companies.name: Gravity Power
companies.what: Hydraulic piston-in-shaft concept (massive piston atop a sealed water column)
companies.signal: Long-gestating; no commercial plant after a decade-plus

variations.white_space: Sparse for physics reasons: lifted-mass energy density is tiny (a 1,000-tonne weight dropped 500 m stores ~1.4 MWh) so steel and civil works dominate cost, and Li-ion's price collapse erased the niche — Energy Vault's own pivot to batteries is the tell; the credible opening is brownfield mine shafts where the structure, grid connection and workforce already exist.

variations.name: Compressed air energy storage (adiabatic & underground caverns)
variations.description: Uses cheap power to compress air into salt caverns, rock caverns or engineered vessels and re-expands it through turbines — modern adiabatic/advanced designs store the compression heat too, eliminating gas burn — enabling 100 MW-to-GW, 6-12+ hour storage at very low cost per kWh.

companies.name: Hydrostor
companies.what: Advanced CAES using water-compensated, purpose-built caverns (no gas, no salt geology required)
companies.signal: $1.76B DOE conditional loan guarantee + $200M from Goldman Sachs/Canada Growth Fund/CPPIB (Feb 2025); 500 MW / 4 GWh Willow Rock (CA) fully permitted Dec 2025, groundbreaking mid-2026; 200 MW / 1.6 GWh Silver City (Broken Hill, Australia) near construction

companies.name: Zhongchu Guoneng (ZCGN)
companies.what: Chinese developer of the world's largest CAES plants using salt caverns
companies.signal: 300 MW / 1,800 MWh Feicheng (Shandong) plant online 2024 at ~$208M (72% efficiency); 700 MW / 4.2 GWh follow-on starting construction 2026

companies.name: Shanghai Electric
companies.what: Supplies the 300 MW-class compression/expansion turbomachinery for China's CAES buildout
companies.signal: First 300 MW unit reached full-load operation Dec 2025, second unit commissioned

companies.name: Uniper (Huntorf)
companies.what: Operates the world's first CAES plant — 321 MW Huntorf, Germany, running since 1978 — proof of cavern longevity
companies.signal: ~47 years of continuous commercial operation

companies.name: Corre Energy
companies.what: Euronext Dublin-listed developer of salt-cavern CAES (and H2 storage) in the Netherlands, Denmark, Germany and Texas
companies.signal: Dutch subsidiary Corre Energy Storage B.V. filed for bankruptcy (Aug 2025); group hired Rothschild to seek investors — in financial distress

companies.name: Augwind Energy
companies.what: AirBattery storing energy via hydraulic compression of air in underground flexible vessels (no caverns needed)
companies.signal: Tel Aviv-listed; multi-MWh pilots in Israel, pursuing grid-scale projects in Germany

companies.name: Cheesecake Energy
companies.what: UK thermo-mechanical CAES (FlexiTanker) packing heat and air storage into repurposed container-scale tanks for distribution-grid sites
companies.signal: Innovate UK-backed; first field pilots underway

variations.name: Liquid air & CO2 battery cycles
variations.description: Liquefies air (or compresses CO2 between a gas dome and liquid tanks in a closed loop) using surplus power, then expands it through turbines to regenerate electricity — siteable anywhere with no caverns or mountains, built from mature industrial-gas hardware.

companies.name: Highview Power
companies.what: Liquid air energy storage (LAES) — cryogenic liquefaction with cold recycle
companies.signal: >GBP 500M raised incl. GBP 300M from UK National Wealth Fund and Centrica (2024); 50 MW / 300 MWh Carrington plant broke ground Nov 2025 for late-2026 operation; 7+ GWh pipeline, two projects advancing in Ofgem's LDES cap-and-floor

companies.name: Energy Dome
companies.what: CO2 Battery — closed thermodynamic cycle between gaseous CO2 in a dome and liquid CO2 tanks; 8-24 hour duration with no critical minerals
companies.signal: First full-scale 20 MW / 200 MWh plant (Ottana, Sardinia) in commercial operation; strategic commercial agreement + equity from Google (Jul 2025); Engie offtake; Alliant Energy project in Wisconsin

companies.name: Phelas
companies.what: Munich startup developing modular, containerized liquid-air storage (Aurora)
companies.signal: Seed-stage; pilot hardware only, little recent public traction

companies.name: Sumitomo SHI FW
companies.what: Sumitomo Heavy Industries arm that invested ~$46M in Highview and acts as LAES EPC/technology partner
companies.signal: Strategic investor since 2020; brings boiler/EPC supply chain

companies.name: Baker Hughes
companies.what: Turbomachinery supplier and strategic investor industrializing Energy Dome's compression-expansion trains
companies.signal: Invested in Energy Dome's Series B; supplies the rotating equipment for CO2 Battery plants

companies.name: MAN Energy Solutions
companies.what: Provides industrial liquefaction and expander technology applicable to LAES plants
companies.signal: Established cryogenic/turbomachinery incumbent partnering on European LDES projects

variations.white_space: Only two credible system leads (Highview, Energy Dome) because these are capex-heavy turbomachinery plants needing bankable EPC wraps, not venture-scale products; the obvious entrants are industrial-gas incumbents (Linde, Air Liquide, Chart) who already make every component and could enter on balance sheet once cap-and-floor-style revenue regimes spread.

variations.name: Pumped storage hydro (conventional, closed-loop, high-density fluid, subsea)
variations.description: Pumps water uphill (or a 2.5x-denser fluid up small hills, or out of pressurized subsea spheres) when power is cheap and runs it back through turbines when needed — at ~180 GW installed it is >90% of the world's storage energy and still the cheapest bulk option where geography allows.

companies.name: Voith Hydro
companies.what: One of three global suppliers of pump-turbines, motor-generators and variable-speed PSH equipment
companies.signal: Equipment in a large share of the world's ~180 GW PSH fleet; major China and Europe orders

companies.name: GE Vernova
companies.what: Hydro division supplying fixed and variable-speed pumped storage units and refurbishments
companies.signal: Active PSH equipment orders across Europe, India and China

companies.name: Andritz
companies.what: Austrian hydro OEM supplying PSH units and modernizations worldwide
companies.signal: Multi-GW PSH order book including European refurbishment wave

companies.name: State Grid Xin Yuan
companies.what: Operates the world's largest pumped-storage fleet, including the 3.6 GW Fengning plant — the biggest on earth
companies.signal: China is building >50 GW of PSH this decade, most under State Grid

companies.name: SSE Renewables
companies.what: Developing Coire Glas (1.5 GW / 30 GWh), Britain's first new large PSH in 40 years
companies.signal: GBP 100M+ pre-FID spend; advancing under UK cap-and-floor LDES regime

companies.name: Drax
companies.what: Expanding the Cruachan underground PSH station in Scotland (+600 MW)
companies.signal: Shortlisted in Ofgem's 2025 LDES cap-and-floor first window

companies.name: rPlus Hydro
companies.what: US pure-play developer of closed-loop PSH (Seminoe, WY ~900 MW; White Pine, NV ~1 GW) with FERC licenses
companies.signal: Two of the most advanced new-build US PSH projects; seeking offtake/financing

companies.name: RheEnergise
companies.what: High-Density Hydro using a fluid 2.5x denser than water so small hills work like mountains
companies.signal: 500 kW grid-connected demonstrator near Plymouth, UK hit peak power Jan 2026; targeting 10-50 MW commercial units

companies.name: Sperra (with Fraunhofer IEE, StEnSea)
companies.what: 3D-printed hollow concrete spheres on the seabed that generate power as water flows in and are pumped empty to recharge
companies.signal: US DOE and German-government-funded; 9 m / 0.5 MW sphere to be deployed off Long Beach, CA by end-2026

companies.name: Ocean Grazer
companies.what: Dutch 'Ocean Battery' storing energy in pressurized bladders on the seabed under offshore wind farms
companies.signal: University of Groningen spinout; concept/pilot stage with limited recent public progress

variations.name: Geomechanical / subsurface pressurized-water storage
variations.description: Pumps water under high pressure into engineered underground rock formations or proppant-held fractures and releases it back through hydropower turbines — using oil-and-gas drilling techniques to put 'pumped hydro' on flat land anywhere, with near-zero standing losses.

companies.name: Quidnet Energy
companies.what: Geomechanical Pumped Storage in shallow rock lenses; the category creator
companies.signal: $10M ARPA-E SCALEUP award; 1 MW / 10 MWh project under 15-year deal with CPS Energy (San Antonio) — demonstrated 35 MWh discharge after six months of pressurized storage with no loss (Jun 2025); backed by Hunt Energy and Breakthrough Energy Ventures

companies.name: Sage Geosystems
companies.what: EarthStore — pressurized water stored in fracture domains of hot dry rock wells, doubling as geothermal generation
companies.signal: 3 MW commercial facility with San Miguel Electric Cooperative (TX); >$97M Series B led by Ormat Technologies (2025); separate 150 MW geothermal deal with Meta

variations.white_space: Essentially two players: reservoir geomechanics is the moat and the risk — fracture containment, cycling fatigue and round-trip efficiency (~50-70%) are unproven at scale, so generalist investors stay away; if Quidnet's CPS project validates economics, oilfield-services firms (Halliburton, SLB-class drilling and pressure-pumping crews) could industrialize deployment almost overnight, making this a natural O&G-transition play.

variations.name: Flywheels
variations.description: Stores electricity as rotational kinetic energy in magnetically levitated rotors that charge and discharge in milliseconds with million-cycle life — a power (not energy) technology that owns UPS and frequency-regulation niches but has repeatedly failed commercially as grid energy storage.

companies.name: Torus
companies.what: Flywheel-plus-battery hybrid systems for data centers, C&I and utility demand response
companies.signal: $200M from Magnetar Capital (Sep 2025); 230+ installations in 2025; PacifiCorp agreements for up to 500 MW of demand-response capacity

companies.name: Beacon Power
companies.what: Built the two flagship 20 MW grid frequency-regulation flywheel plants (Stephentown NY, Hazle PA)
companies.signal: Chapter 11 in 2011 despite working hardware; assets to Rockland Capital (2012), later sold to Convergent — 'the hardware worked, the business did not'

companies.name: Amber Kinetics
companies.what: Four-hour steel-rotor flywheels (32 kWh KESS) — the only long-duration flywheel attempt
companies.signal: 17 years old with only ~$25-47M disclosed funding; US military microgrid evaluations (Miramar Q3 2025, Viejas 2026) but living on grants, not sales

companies.name: VYCON (Calnetix)
companies.what: Kinetic-energy UPS flywheels widely deployed in data centers, hospitals and crane regeneration
companies.signal: Thousands of units fielded; profitable power-quality niche

companies.name: Piller Power Systems (incl. ex-Active Power)
companies.what: Rotary UPS and flywheel ride-through systems; absorbed distressed flywheel maker Active Power (2016)
companies.signal: Langley Holdings unit; standard kit for mission-critical facilities

companies.name: Revterra
companies.what: Passive magnetic-bearing 'kinetic batteries' (100 kWh / 400 kW) buffering EV fast-charging on weak grids
companies.signal: $6M seed (2022); pilot deployments with charging developers

companies.name: QuinteQ Energy
companies.what: Lightweight Boeing-derived flywheels for port cranes, military microgrids and peak shaving
companies.signal: Dutch; deployments at ports and defense sites, early commercial

companies.name: Stornetic
companies.what: German DuraStor flywheel arrays for rail braking energy and grid services
companies.signal: Quiet in recent years; commercial traction unclear

variations.white_space: As energy storage the physics is unforgiving — self-discharge and the $/kWh of spinning steel confine flywheels to seconds-to-minutes, and the corporate graveyard (Beacon Ch.11, Active Power distressed sale, Pentadyne liquidation, Temporal Power) proves grid arbitrage never penciled; the live opening is power-quality hybrids that shield batteries from cycling (Torus's model) and inertia-as-a-service on inverter-heavy grids.

variations.name: Hydrogen power-to-power LDES (electrolyzer + cavern/tank + fuel cell or turbine)
variations.description: Converts surplus renewable electricity to hydrogen via electrolysis, stores it in salt caverns, tanks or metal hydrides for days to seasons, and converts it back through fuel cells or hydrogen-capable turbines — the only practical seasonal storage, though sub-40% round-trip efficiency makes it expensive without mandates.

companies.name: ACES Delta (Mitsubishi Power + Chevron JV)
companies.what: World's largest green-H2 storage hub: 220 MW electrolysis plus two 4.5-million-barrel salt caverns in Delta, Utah feeding IPP's 840 MW 30%-hydrogen combined cycle
companies.signal: $504M DOE loan guarantee; all 40 electrolyzers installed and run at 100% load by Feb 2026, project ~95% complete and commissioning

companies.name: Mitsubishi Power Americas
companies.what: Supplies the hydrogen-capable M501JAC turbines and integrates the IPP Renewed / ACES power-to-power chain (30% H2 now, 100% by 2045)
companies.signal: Anchor OEM for the flagship US hydrogen LDES project

companies.name: Chevron
companies.what: Acquired Magnum Development (owner of the Utah salt-cavern site) in 2023 to co-own ACES Delta — an oil major buying into H2 storage
companies.signal: Holds majority interest in ACES Delta alongside Mitsubishi Power

companies.name: HDF Energy
companies.what: Renewstable baseload plants combining solar, 16 MW electrolysis, 128 MWh H2 storage and fuel cells for island grids
companies.signal: Euronext-listed; CEOG French Guiana — the world's first multi-MW hydrogen power plant — in final equipment installation 2025, serving ~10,000 households

companies.name: Energy Vault (Calistoga Resiliency Center)
companies.what: Owns/operates the world's first ultra-long-duration hybrid hydrogen-fuel-cell + battery microgrid (8.5 MW / 293 MWh) replacing diesel for PG&E wildfire shutoffs
companies.signal: Commercial operation Sep 2025 under 10.5-year PG&E tolling agreement

companies.name: Plug Power
companies.what: PEM electrolyzers, fuel cells and stationary power for hydrogen P2P chains
companies.signal: NASDAQ-listed; closed $1.66B DOE loan guarantee (Jan 2025) amid sustained losses, layoffs and cash concerns

companies.name: GKN Hydrogen
companies.what: Metal-hydride solid-state H2 storage (16x density of compressed gas, 30-year life) packaged as power-to-power microgrid systems
companies.signal: Acquired by Langley Holdings from Dowlais Group (Aug 2024) into its Power Solutions division; 7,000+ cycles proven at 99% efficiency

companies.name: Siemens Energy
companies.what: Silyzer electrolyzers plus hydrogen-capable gas turbines; ran HYFLEXPOWER, the first integrated industrial power-to-H2-to-power demo at 100% hydrogen
companies.signal: 100% H2 turbine operation demonstrated in France (2023); H2-ready turbine line shipping

variations.white_space: Round-trip efficiency of ~30-40% plus electrolyzer capex means no merchant business case exists — every operating project leans on a mandate (Calistoga wildfire resilience), an island grid with diesel-price competition (CEOG), or policy-backed utility offtake (LADWP/IPP); the structural opening is pairing existing or cheap-to-mine salt caverns with the H2-capable turbine fleets utilities are already buying, rather than greenfield fuel-cell plants.
